summaries.week-3-section: The Team Start-Up Competition requires students to adopt a real early-stage startup, interview its founder, and pitch it at Demo Day, accounting for 20% of the course grade.

week-3-section.text: The competition is worth 20% of the course grade, plus 5% for the founder interview.

summaries.week-3-section: The founder interview is a graded checkpoint where the entire team participates in a 30–60 minute discussion with the startup's founder or a tech professional.

week-3-section.text: The interview should be 30–60 minutes, conducted on Zoom or in person, with every team member present.
The deliverable requires 3 slides and a 5–7 minute presentation with equal speaking time.
Teams should prepare 4–5 core questions, with one person moderating and one taking notes.
Suggested starting points include asking how the Berkeley ecosystem helped build the company or walking through the fundraising process.
Each team member must ask at least one question, and the team must assign a moderator and a notetaker before the call.

links.title: Founder Outreach

summaries.week-3-section: Effective outreach to busy founders requires a professional, targeted approach, and students must begin this process immediately.

week-3-section.text: Founders can be reached via SkyDeck company pages, LinkedIn with a specific note, or the YC company page founder profiles.
The outreach email must be professional, stating who the students are, why they chose the company, and proposing two specific times for a 30–45 minute Zoom call.
It is advised to line up a backup person early because founder replies can take 2–3 weeks.
